sources.citation: Edwards 2021, Rote-Meto Comparative Dictionary, ANU Press, ch.2 Rote phonology incl. Tii (full PDF read)
sources.quote: Content words contain at least two vowels. Some functors, such as the conjunction ma 'and', are monosyllabic. Stress falls on the penultimate vowel of a word with secondary stress assigned to every second syllable to the left.

sources.citation: Tamelan, Thersia. 2021. A grammar of Dela: an Austronesian language of Rote, eastern Indonesia. PhD thesis, The Australian National University. hdl.handle.net/1885/250953 (550 pp.)
sources.quote: For Dela (dela1251, West Rote; NOT Tii): 'Word stress in Dela falls on the penultimate syllable of the root. Since each vowel is a syllable nucleus, it is the penultimate segmental vowel that carries the stress. Roots with two metrical feet have secondary stress on the initial syllable. ... Affixes, partial reduplication, enclitics (including sentence/phrasal enclitics) and paragogic vowels are extrametrical ... and stress does not shift.' p.38: 'trisyllabic and quadrisyllabic affixed and reduplicated words do not have secondary stresses.' Stress realised by pitch, intensity, duration.
sources.note: Nearest modern full grammar in western Rote and the source behind Edwards' Rote-wide stress sentence; its root-penult + extrametrical-clitic + no-secondary-on-prefixes analysis (pp.36-38) is the best guide to what the Tii 'domain' field (currently UNCODED) and the secondary-stress tail should say.

sources.citation: Jonker, J. C. G. 1913. Bijdrage tot de kennis der Rottineesche tongvallen. Bijdragen tot de Taal-, Land- en Volkenkunde van Nederlandsch-Indie 68: 521-622. doi 10.1163/22134379-90001774 (archive.org item dli.ministry.10288, djvu scanned text)
sources.quote: None for Ti/Tii. The only 'klemtoon' in the article concerns the pronunciation of the author name Manafe (p.521). The Ti section treats retention of r and medial nd, mb for Ba'a mp, pronoun forms ai/ei, past particle ena, 3sg verb form ifada (vs nafada elsewhere) and Ti's closeness to Lole; Jonker defers grammar (incl. accent) to the 'ter perse zijnde' Spraakkunst (1915), whose sec. 4 states the rule for 'het Rottineesch' as a whole.
sources.locator: pp.521-540 (dialect survey; 'Het dialect van Ti' passage ca. pp.533-535)
